description: Executions whose expiry time is exactly equal to either the start or the end bound of the window are excluded, so only expiry times strictly between the two bounds count.

c.request: For order executions with an expiry time (`expirespot`) between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' (comparing the values as text), group them by order (`ordersmark`) and work out each order's average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`, ignoring missing values) and its number of executions. Then give me one row with the average of those per-order averages (ignoring missing ones) and the total of the per-order execution counts, without rounding. Executions whose expiry time is exactly equal to either the start or the end bound of the window are excluded, so only expiry times strictly between the two bounds count.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_remain) AS avg_of_avg_remaincount, SUM(exec_count) AS total_executions FROM (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) AS per_order

d.request: Among order executions whose expiry time (`expirespot`, compared as text) is strictly greater than '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and strictly less than '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' (both bounds excluded), group by order (`ordersmark`) to get each order's average `remaincount` (ignoring nulls) and execution count, then return one row with the unrounded average of those per-order averages (ignoring nulls) and the sum of the per-order execution counts.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_remain) AS avg_of_avgs, SUM(exec_count) AS total_exec_count FROM (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) AS t

b.request: Executions whose `expirespot`, compared as text, is strictly greater than '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and strictly less than '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' (both bounds excluded), grouped by `ordersmark`, with each order's average `remaincount` (NULLs ignored) and its execution count, then one row giving the unrounded average of those per-order averages (NULLs ignored) and the sum of the per-order execution counts.
b.sql: SELECT CAST(ordersmark AS TEXT) AS ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remaincount, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark UNION ALL SELECT NULL, AVG(avg_rc), SUM(cnt) FROM (SELECT AVG(remaincount) AS avg_rc, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM orderexecutions WHERE CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) t

a.request: Looking only at order executions whose expiry time (`expirespot`) falls between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', with both endpoints excluded (comparing the values as text), group them by order (`ordersmark`) and, for each order, compute the average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`, ignoring missing values) and the number of executions. Then give me one row with the average of those per-order averages (ignoring missing ones) and the total of the per-order execution counts, without rounding.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_remain) AS avg_of_avg_remaincount, SUM(exec_count) AS total_executions FROM (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) > '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) < '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) AS per_order
